title: Sparsity and pruning
brief: Score weights by magnitude and by Wanda, build and compress a 2:4 mask, and check the temperature-scaled distillation loss with a finite-difference gradient. A PyTorch semi-structured check runs only on CUDA.
hints: Wanda scores are abs(W) times the L2 norm of each input channel over the calibration tokens. The norm is one number per column, shared by every output row.
prune_rowwise compares weights inside one output row. Sort the scores with stable=True so a tie drops the lower index first.
A 2:4 group is four consecutive input columns. Keep the two highest scores. Check the mask with a count per group of four, not with the overall density.
Compressed 2:4 stores two values and two 2-bit positions per group of four, in ascending column order. Use the mask, because a kept weight can be 0.

kd_loss is T squared times the batch mean of KL(softmax(teacher/T) || softmax(student/T)). The gradient with respect to the student logits is T times (p_student - p_teacher) divided by the batch size.
sparse_semi_structured_check returns None on a CPU. It was never run on a GPU.
